body: The Foshay Tower, the 32-story Art Deco landmark in downtown Minneapolis that houses the 229-room W Minneapolis hotel, is scheduled for a foreclosure sale on December 18, 2026, Connect CRE reported, citing the Minneapolis/St. Paul Business Journal. The sale follows an August 25, 2026 ruling by a Hennepin County District Court judge that the tower's owner owes more than $42.3 million on a defaulted loan on the property at 821 S. Marquette Ave.

Deutsche Bank filed the foreclosure complaint as trustee for bondholders in an affiliated commercial mortgage-backed securities trust, Weekly Real Estate News reported in April 2026, citing the Star Tribune. The suit alleged that the owners failed to pay off a $51 million mortgage that matured in May 2025, and asked the court to appoint a receiver to manage the property and to award roughly $43 million in unpaid principal, interest and fees.

The tower was built in 1929 as the headquarters of utilities magnate Wilbur Foshay. It was Minneapolis's tallest building until the IDS Center was built in 1972, was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1978, and was converted from offices into a W hotel in 2008, according to Weekly Real Estate News.

timeline.label: Foshay Tower is completed as the headquarters of Wilbur Foshay's utilities business
The tower is converted from offices into a W hotel
The $51M mortgage matures without being paid off
Deutsche Bank, as CMBS trustee, sues to foreclose in Hennepin County District Court and asks for a receiver
A Hennepin County judge rules the owner owes more than $42.3M on the defaulted loan
Foreclosure sale of the Foshay Tower scheduled
